title: Slice-and-stitch eviction safelist with kernel-hint routing for paged KV
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: In high-concurrency paged-attention workloads we observe suboptimal reuse and high rehydration cost when fragmented KV pages are evicted. Evictions often remove small slices that are expensive to restore, causing repeated decode stalls and kernel teardowns. Goal: reduce end-to-end tail latency and token decode cost by introducing a low-overhead eviction safelist (slice-and-stitch), compact allocation heuristics, and kernel-hint routing so that hot fragments are allocated and decoded in kernel-friendly placements.
background: Current allocator is LRU-like per-shard with coarse slab buckets. When pressure spikes we evict small fragments scattered across slabs. Restoring these fragments during prefill causes many tiny CUDA kernel launches, increased PCIe traffic for staged restores, and KV cache churn. Existing optimizations (batch prefill, background compaction) help but don't capture stitchable slices or inform kernel scheduler about locality. Similar problems observed in ENG-772000 and ENG-611223 but both focused on eviction windows; this ticket takes a different angle: proactive safelists and kernel-aware placement.
goals: 1) Implement an eviction safelist that marks 'stitchable' slices that can be retained on-heap and cheaply reconstructed on GPU. 2) Add compact-stride allocator that prefers contiguous micro-slices up to 4KB to reduce fragmentation. 3) Extend kernel routing to accept placement hints so decode kernels are scheduled on GPUs where neighboring fragments reside. 4) Integrate prefill scheduling to opportunistically reorder prefill to stitch safelisted slices before heavy decode waves.
technical_approach:
- Eviction Safelist: maintain a lightweight per-shard Bloom+LRU index of fragment checksums and metadata (length, adjacent offsets). On eviction, instead of freeing raw bytes, we record a safelist entry if the fragment is contiguous with at least one neighbor and predicted reuse score > threshold. Safelist entries are stored compressed on host mem and referenced by an ID that can be used during prefill to reconstruct KV slice via a single microcopy+kernel call.
- Compact-Stride Allocator: micro-block allocator that prefers stride sizes aligned to tile boundaries; when allocating, attempt coalescing of adjacent requests into contiguous micro-slices; reclamation runs opportunistically to coalesce free fragments into larger stitchable regions.
- Kernel-Hint Routing: add an optional placement hint field to decode scheduling (hot/cold/neighbor-hot) so the runtime can preferentially schedule decode kernels on GPU that hold adjacent fragments. If hint unavailable, use current policy.
- Prefill Scheduler Integration: a short window prefill hedging policy that reorders pending prefills to prioritize constructing stitchable safelist groups, reducing subsequent individual restores. Scheduler uses a small priority queue keyed by reuse prediction and contiguity score.
- Fallbacks: safelist is advisory; if storage pressure high, safelist entries can be dropped. Kernel hint is a soft hint and does not violate capacity-aware routing.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tail 99th token latency for target workload (multi-tenant chat + long context) decreases by >= 18% in lab runs.
- Average restore-related extra kernel launches per 1M tokens reduced by >= 35%.
- End-to-end cost per token (GPU time + host restores) reduced by >= 10% on our internal benchmark suite.
- No regression in stability: no increase in OOM/gc events in stress tests.
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and can be rolled back remotely.

testing_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator coalescing, safelist admission and expiry.
- Microbench: synthetic KV restore microbench measuring kernel counts and copy sizes.
- Integration: end-to-end decode benchmark using multi-tenant traces (chat, summarization, retrieval-augmented).
- Stress: long-run GC/eviction stress with competing tenants to ensure safelist doesn't grow unbounded.
- Fuzz restore paths for mismatched fragment checksums and simulated partial failures.
monitoring_and_metrics:
- Metrics to add: safelist_admits, safelist_evictions, safelist_restores, stitch_restore_latency_ms, kernel_launches_per_restore, restore_bytes_transferred, allocator_fragmentation_ratio.
- Dashboards: per-shard safelist hit rate, tail decode latency correlated with safelist hit/miss.
- Alerts: safelist size growth > 5x baseline for > 15m, restored fragment checksum mismatch rate > 0.01%.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: safelist added host memory pressure. Mitigation: strict size quota per tenant + decay policy.
- Risk: kernel hint increases scheduling complexity and may reduce overall throughput. Mitigation: fallback to current scheduler and measure queue length impact; limit hints to top 10% hot fragments.
- Risk: stitching restores may be incorrect under concurrent writes. Mitigation: versioned fragment IDs and atomic install protocol during prefill.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag off by default in runtime. 2) Canary on 1 rack in staging with internal traffic. 3) If stable, enable for 5% of internal tenants for 48h, run perf regressions. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% with automatic rollback guardrails based on latency and safelist metrics.
notes:
- This approach intentionally keeps safelist entries resumable so we avoid long blocking compaction runs.
- We expect the largest wins for workloads with token-span reuse > 32 tokens and moderate fragmentation (many small fragments < 8KB).
- If results are good, follow-up ticket will add a lightweight ML predictor for reuse score.
